Title: A novel mixed technique for order abatement in linear time invariant systems and robustness analysis of DC motor

DC motor
Priyajit Dash1, M. L. Meena1, M. Ramkumar Raja2 & Wahaj Ahmad Khan3
This work presents a novel mixed technique for order abatement (OA) of linear time-invariant (LTI) 
systems. The proposed approach utilizes the Honey Badger algorithm (HBA) to compute the numerator 
polynomials, while the stability equation (SE) method determines the denominator polynomials of 
the abated system (AS). The Integral of squared error (ISE) is employed as the objective function to 
minimize the error between the high-order system (HOS) and the AS, ensuring accurate coefficient 
estimation. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed mixed approach, various performance 
and transient parameters were compared against well-established techniques from the literature. 
The results from tested examples demonstrate the superior accuracy and stability of the proposed 
method in approximating system dynamics. Additionally, the study explores the implementation of 
an HBA-tuned PID controller for DC motor speed control, with the integral of time-weighted absolute 
error (ITAE) serving as the objective function. A robustness analysis was conducted by varying the 
motor parameters, and the transient response of the HBA/PID technique was compared with existing 
methods. The findings reveal that HBA/PID achieves lower rise time and settling time, leading to an 
overall improvement in the motor’s response. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed 
approach in both order abatement and robust control applications.
Keywords  Stability equation, Honey Badger algorithm, Order abatement, Abated system, DC motor, PID 
controller, Robustness analysis
Most of the science and engineering application-related systems are very complex. It is very difficult to deal 
with such a complex system1. Hence there is a need for order abatement of the complex system. The AS must 
retain the important inherent properties of complex system/ Original (HOS) with minimal error. The AS 
becomes easier to handle than complex/ HOS also simulation time and cost are reduced. The OA can be done by 
conventional techniques, optimization techniques, and mixed techniques where the numerator and denominator 
can be determined by different techniques to have effective results. OA by using conventional techniques are 
suggested in the literature such as Stability equation2, Hankel Approximations3, Routh Approximation4, Pade 
Approximation5, Pole Clustering6. Other conventional techniques are available in the literature7–11. OA by 
using optimization techniques are available in the literature such as Invasive Weed Optimization12, Differential 
Evolution13, Flower Pollination Algorithm14, Modified Cuckoo Search15, Harmony Search16, Bonobo Optimizer17 
also, other optimization techniques are available in the literature18–22.
OA by using mixed techniques where the numerator and denominator of AS are calculated separately by 
various existing techniques in the literature such as23 suggested a mixed technique for determining the AS of 
Single Input Single Output (SISO) and also it can also apply to Multiple Input–Multiple Output (MIMO) LTI

Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA)
The proposed HBA imitates the foraging behavior of Honey Badger (HB). This creature loves honey, and it is 
popular for its fearlessness and intelligence in nature. It likes to remain alone in self-dug holes and meets the 
other HB when desires to have a mate. This animal has two different manners of foraging. One manner is to find 
the prey it looks for by its sense of smell. But it is not enough to smell honey this stage is called the digging stage. 
Hence getting honey is another way additional birds are called guiding birds it needs when it looks for honey. 
With the assistance of guiding birds, it gets honey too. This manner of getting the honey with the assistance of 
a guiding bird is called the honey stage42–44. HBA mimics the behavior of HB in nature. This mimics behavior 
has been utilized for OA of large-scale dynamic systems. The HBA has been chosen in this work because of 
its excellent exploration–exploitation balance, which guarantees precise low-order approximations, the HBA is 
perfect for AS. It offers versatile objective function selection such as ISE, ITAE, and global optimization, avoiding 
local minima. Compared to conventional approaches, HBA provides robust performance, handles complicated 
and nonlinear systems with ease, and increases computational efficiency. It is better at abating the HOS while 
preserving accuracy and stability because of its stochastic and adaptive character.

Assumptions  The following assumptions have been considered during the Simulation.
System Stability—The original and AS remain stable.
Linearity—The system is linear and time-invariant (LTI) for valid reduction.
Bounded Search Space—Coefficients are restricted within predefined limits.
Error Metrics—Accuracy is evaluated considering ISE as an objective function.
Standard Inputs—Simulations use step input with zero initial conditions.
Computational Feasibility—HBA is assumed to converge efficiently. No External Disturbances, Noise, and 
real-world uncertainties are ignored.
Validity of Reduction—The retains essential system dynamics.

Benefits and drawbacks of HBA
Benefits of HBA
•	 Improved Accuracy: The HBA optimizes reduced-order model parameters to closely match the original sys­
tem.
•	 Global Search Capability: Unlike traditional reduction techniques, HBA avoids local optima and explores the 
entire solution space.
•	 Automatic Tuning: HBA automatically adjusts coefficients without requiring manual selection.
•	 Versatility: Applicable to various types of dynamic systems.
•	 Robustness: Handles nonlinearity and high-order models effectively.
Drawbacks of HBA
•	 Computational Cost: Optimization-based approaches require more computation compared to other meth­
ods.
•	 Parameter Sensitivity: Performance depends on the proper selection of algorithm parameters (e.g., popula­
tion size, exploration rates).
•	 Convergence Speed: May require many iterations to achieve an optimal solution.
•	 Implementation Complexity: Requires additional coding effort compared to traditional MOR techniques

Conclusion
In this work, Higher-order LTI systems have been modeled using the proposed mixed technique, with ISE 
considered as the objective function for OA. To compare the applicability of the proposed approach, three 
HOS were examined. AS of Previously existing techniques have been compared with the AS of the proposed 
technique from the literature. In all three HOS, the Performance and the Transient parameters obtained through 
the simulation were then compared with those obtained from other existing techniques Also, the OA with the 
proposed mixed approach was calculated and compared to the conventional techniques, indicating a very good 
estimation of both Step Response and Frequency Response. The Proposed technique has a lower ISE value than 
existing techniques in all three systems also it is found that AS is stable if the original HOS is stable. In the case of 
speed control of the DC motor, the HBA/PID method has been used with the aid of the ITAE objective function. 
A robustness analysis was conducted by altering the DC motor parameters, with the transient parameters 
compared accordingly. After tuning the HBA, it is evident that changes in the DC motor’s parameters do not 
affect the functionality of the PID controller.
